notes: Two conditional conjunctions (אִם, כִּי) stand against one written *if*: אִם, at the clause head where the English word stands, takes it and כִּי is unrepresented under rules 22 and 42.

מִצְוֺת is given the whole recasting *the things ... hath commanded*, headed on *commanded*; the alternative confines it to *the things* and marks *hath commanded* added, which rule 20's supplied-lexical-verb clause would then have to license — rejected because the noun's own lexeme is what the English verb states.
One *any* stands against אַחַת and כֹּל; it is given to אַחַת, where the English word stands, and כֹּל is unrepresented.
